name: OrderFactory permissionless createOrderForBuyer drains buyer escrow
summary: The 2017 order factory's createOrder entry (0xbde886fc) checked only that the named buyer had an active request, not who called it. Any caller could open an order for any buyer with itself as seller; the factory moved the buyer's whole Account System ETH balance into the order, and the seller-gated abort sent it to the attacker. Dormant buyer balances were drained in 2026.
notes: Reset is the Account System's grant to this factory (36b196cf, slot 0x6f8fc102.. 0->1), four blocks after the factory's deployment: with that slot zeroed the factory's balance transfer (0x506d994b) reverts. The operator's per-buyer registrations are live user data, not resets.

Campaign: the attacker's four further drains in the same block, its drain of the byte-different sibling deployment (factory 0xf682e127, Account System 0xcccbeac8, 0.18 ETH) and a later copycat (0xfc3facd6, 0.011 ETH). Loss is the two Account Systems' net ETH outflow per tx; the attacker's top-up deposits net out. A trace_filter scan found no non-operator createOrder call before the anchor.
Factory, Account System and order templates are unverified; the mechanism comes from traces, an unprivileged eth_call of 0xbde886fc that succeeds, and the DeFiHackLabs reproduction.
